title: Tenant-configurable eligibility wizard for hosted streaming with contract-aware fallbacks
creator: Priya Natarajan
description: Enterprise customers frequently submit hosted API feature requests that combine streaming chat, function/tool calling, and structured outputs. They expect deterministic eligibility checks (SLA tiers, data residency, contract clauses) and automated fallbacks when requests violate contract or security policies. This ticket proposes a tenant-configurable eligibility wizard that runs during intake to surface required contract terms, enforce per-tenant policy gates, and generate contract-aware fallback plans (e.g., disable tool calls, force structured schemas, route to dedicated capacity). The goal is to reduce manual triage time for PMs/support, improve onboarding decision consistency, and prevent rework during implementation. The wizard must be accessible via the internal intake UI and callable via an intake API for channel integrations.
acceptance_criteria: Eligibility wizard prototype available in internal intake UI that accepts request payload (chat/streaming/toolcalls/structured) and returns a pass/fail with reasons
Wizard supports configurable tenant policies for: allowed tool categories, minimum SLA tier, data residency constraints, mandatory structured outputs, and required contract addenda

When a request fails eligibility, wizard returns a recommended fallback plan (one of: enforce structured output, disable tool calls, require routing to Dedicated/Private, or propose contract amendment) with cost/latency delta estimates
Audit log records every eligibility decision with tenant ID, rule matched, operator who modified policy, and timestamp
API endpoint documented and covered by integration tests (>= 80% unit coverage) and an end-to-end smoke test against intake flow
Telemetry and dashboard for PMs showing distribution of failures by rule, and top 10 tenants triggering fallbacks
rollout_plan: Phase 1 (2 weeks): Internal prototype wired into intake UI; limited policy controls stored in feature flag-backed tenant config; gather PM/support feedback
Phase 2 (3 weeks): Expand policy expression, add API endpoint, integrate cost/latency estimator microservice, add audit logs and telemetry
Phase 3 (2 weeks): Pilot with two enterprise customers via manual opt-in; gather real signal and adjust fallback heuristics
Phase 4 (1 week): Gradual enable by tenant with admin-only toggle and compliance sign-off; documentation and runbook handoff to GTM and Support
metrics: Reduce PM/manual triage time per request from mean 2.5 days to < 8 hours for pilot tenants
Fraction of intake requests auto-classified (pass or fallback) >= 70% in pilot
Number of requests routed to Dedicated/Private because of eligibility decisions
Dashboard: rule-level failure rate and false-positive rate (target < 10%)
risks: Overly conservative rules could block valid requests, harming conversion for self-serve customers
Incorrect cost/latency estimates could lead to suboptimal fallback suggestions
Policy complexity may require UI/UX work to avoid admin confusion
Security review may block rollout for certain enforcement actions (e.g., auto-disabling toolcalls)
notes: Design lead: align on a compact policy DSL we can store per tenant in config store
Engineering: reuse existing routing decision service and cost estimator microservice to avoid duplicating logic
Legal: require contract template for any recommendation that suggests contract amendment; legal review flagged
Observe: tie telemetry events to intake request IDs so we can replay decisions during postmortem
